case_name: SRL-2018 Remote Desktop Server RD-06 — Memory Forensics
description: Volatility3 memory analysis. 0 LOTL processes + code injection in 4 processes. Minimal compromise — payload deployed but no active C2 at acquisition time. Likely a propagation target at the periphery of the attack.
devil_advocate: 4 injected processes with 0 LOTL could represent JIT compilation artifacts or legitimate security software injection. No active C2 indicator at acquisition time.

artifacts.content: vol3 windows.malfind: code injection in 4 processes (PIDs: 3996, 112, 400, 00). PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE regions. Windows 10 Enterprise. No LOTL processes detected via pslist — payload dormant or beacon in long sleep cycle at acquisition.
forensic_anomalies: 4 injected processes with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE — same shellcode signature as all other compromised SRL-2018 hosts
Absence of active LOTL despite 4 injections: beacon may be in long sleep (hours/days) at 2018-09-07 acquisition time, or active LOTL terminated between infection and snapshot
Low injection count (4) vs other RD servers (12-43) positions RD-06 as peripheral propagation target — attacker allocated minimal resources to this host

artifacts.content: vol3 windows.pslist: 0 living-off-the-land processes at acquisition time. Process list analyzed — no active cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or other LOLBAS anomalies in running state. Injected code present in memory but not executing via LOTL at snapshot time.
forensic_anomalies: Injected payload (4 processes confirmed by malfind) is dormant — shellcode present but beacon not calling out at acquisition time
Dormant payload is a deliberate attacker OpSec choice: reduced network noise while maintaining persistence for future activation
0 LOTL with 4 injections is the lowest activity signature in the compromised RD server set — consistent with attacker treating RD-06 as a reserve/fallback pivot

artifacts.content: vol3 windows.netscan: no established external connections at acquisition. Internal network connectivity expected via RDP (3389) and SMB (445) from RD-04 (primary pivot). Absence of external C2 connections consistent with dormant beacon state — payload injected but outbound communication suppressed.
forensic_anomalies: No external connections despite confirmed code injection: attacker deployed payload but has not yet activated external C2 on this host
Dormant + no external connections + 4 injections: classic sleeper compromise — attacker pre-positioned on RD-06 for future use if primary pivots (RD-04, RD-01) are detected
RD-06 dormant state increases forensic difficulty: standard network-based detection (IDS/IPS) would not alert on this host despite confirmed compromise

artifacts.content: Corpus context: RD-06 is 5th of 5 compromised RD servers. Compromise chain: admin -> AV -> RD-04 (hub) -> RD-01, RD-03, RD-05, RD-06 (propagated). LARIAT C2 logs confirm systematic RD server sweep from hub at RD-04. RD-06 infected last in the sequence — explains minimal investment (4 injections, 0 active LOTL).
forensic_anomalies: 5/6 RD servers systematically compromised confirms deliberate sweep, not random propagation — attacker enumerated all available RD servers from hub
RD-06 last in infection sequence: attacker priorities were RD-01 (12 LOTL) and RD-04 (30 LOTL) first, spreading to RD-06 as final redundancy
Even dormant compromise provides attacker with persistence: if primary C2 pivots are cleaned, dormant RD-06 payload can be reactivated without re-exploitation

peirce_chain.firstness: RD server in compromised network — propagation target
peirce_chain.secondness: Code injection in 4 processes confirmed — same attacker toolset as RD-01/03/04/05
peirce_chain.thirdness: Minimal footprint (0 LOTL, 4 injections) positions RD-06 as a peripheral propagation target. Attacker spread payload broadly across all RD servers but concentrated C2 activity on RD-04.
